📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

Industry observers note that but the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a massive amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he noted.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

It has been revealed that there's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ indicates Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

Industry observers note that ‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that indicates in his play,' states Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against Latest Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

Industry observers note that to make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that indicates in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

Sources indicate that ‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

Sources indicate that there is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

AC Milan are looking to start a Europa League comeback, if you will, in Greece tomorrow against an Olympiacos side who are flying.

In a recent development, from their last trip to Olympiacos, Milan know that getting three points tomorrow night will not be easy. Unfortunately, it comes at a time when they really do need easy points.

In terms of qualifying for the knockout phase, their best hopes are presently finishing in the top 24 and getting through the Round of 16 knockout tie. However, a win on Thursday could open hopes of a top eight finish….

➤ Manager: Imanol Alguacil Barrenetxea ➤ Form (all comps): W-W-D-D-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Hezze, Yaremchuk, Gonzalez – 1 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Freuler, Chiquinho – 1 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

Olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

According to recent reports, the spending was almost totally offset by four substantial sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

In a recent development, mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the newly introduced head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are presently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

According to recent reports, in the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey is the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

Sources indicate that in defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical concerns, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

Forest head into their upcoming game sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, seven points adrift of their eighth-placed opponents.

While Forest's underlying statistics in the final third have been encouraging, individual mistakes have sometimes cost them.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Glasner acknowledged that Forest's players must perform better in many areas of their game.

Recent findings suggest that the Austrian told reporters: "We’ve been talking a lot about running here. You can see we’ve climbed the bottom of the table. We are starting to be in mid-table with all these stats. I think we can see this progression.

"The physical – especially the running stats – are getting more and more competitive. You don’t need to be a heavyweight boxer in our squad. But you need to anticipate. You need to be quick in legs and in mind.".

In a recent development, when addressing other problems, he added: "We all thought and wished we would have more points. Performances in many games were better than results. We wanted and expected more from us to be honest.

"We have to accept the reality. I’m no magician. I have no magic dust I can spread. We need to improve our individual mistakes.

"We need to improve our efficiency in attack. Still no goals from set pieces. I think I always talked about stability and consistency. This is what we still have to find and do better.

"To really perform consistently on a high level, we get enough points and we get enough wins. Then you climb the table and this is what we’re looking for.".

After the 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United, Alonso gave a dismissive answer when a reporter claimed that Chelsea were unable to cope physically against the majority of Premier League teams.

However, it has been clear to supporters that Chelsea possess a team that struggle on that front, with decision-making and in front of goal.

Add in the frequent individual mistakes and you get a similar team to Forest, albeit one that is less physically-imposing.

There is an argument that Chelsea are the perfect opponents for Forest to return to form.

Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant.
  • In a recent development, the move, which has yet to be publicly confirmed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play.
  • The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association stated the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

In a recent development, the move, which has yet to be publicly confirmed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF said it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey.".

In a recent development, as of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," said Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Recent findings suggest that how this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been said about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days.".

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

Sources indicate that "We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who remarked he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

According to recent reports, "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could problem visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions right now in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," noted spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius said he didn't wish to "speculate on implications.".

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the issue could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The fresh supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit indicated Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

Sources indicate that the offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

It has been revealed that the spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering newly introduced players on its UEFA List A.

Sources indicate that those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

  • The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt their alarming slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Konyaspor to GAIN Park on Friday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.

Alanyaspor have endured a difficult period in recent weeks, losing five consecutive league matches and leaving themselves increasingly vulnerable to being dragged into the relegation battle.

The Thunders began that sequence with a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce before suffering a 2-1 home loss against Kocaelispor six days later, and their struggles continued when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, suffering a humiliating 5-0 defeat, which was followed by a 2-0 home loss to Trabzonspor.

Those results led to Joao Pereira leaving by mutual agreement, with Ugur Ucar subsequently appointed, but the newly introduced manager was unable to bring about an immediate improvement as Alanyaspor were beaten 2-1 at Kasimpasa in his first game in charge.

They have now lost five Super Lig matches in a row and are without a win in their last six, drawing one, leaving Ucar with plenty to address as his side attempt to rediscover the form that helped them collect points earlier in the campaign.

Their recent performances have also been particularly disappointing defensively, having conceded 12 goals across their last five league matches, making them the worst-performing side in the division over that period.

The 4-1 victory over 12 Bingolspor in the Turkish Cup is the only positive result the Thunders have recorded during that spell, and just their second home win across all competitions, having won only their opening home league game, drawn two and lost two, leaving them without a league victory on home soil in their last four attempts.

However, Alanyaspor have enjoyed the better of recent meetings between the sides, remaining unbeaten in their last six competitive encounters with Konyaspor while winning each of the last five.

Konyaspor, meanwhile, have also struggled to maintain consistency this season and are four points behind the hosts, having collected just two wins, two draws and eight defeats from their opening 12 league matches.

Ilhan Palut's side have also lost their last three league games, suffering a heavy 4-0 home defeat against Galatasaray before losing 1-0 away to Samsunspor and then 4-2 against Besiktas in their latest outing.

Aside from their poor record in this fixture, the Anatolian Eagles have another concern heading into Friday's encounter, having collected just one point from five away matches this season.

In fact, Konyaspor have failed to score in their last four away matches, losing three of those games by a 1-0 scoreline, with a goalless draw against Kasimpasa coming between those defeats.

The Anatolian side have also failed to win on their last three visits to Alanyaspor, losing the previous two by 2-1 scorelines after drawing 2-2 on their earlier trip.

Alanyaspor form (all competitions):.

Konyaspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Alanyaspor will be without Fidan Aliti, who is suspended for Friday's encounter, leaving Ucar with a defensive selection concern ahead of the match.

Fatih Aksoy and Paolo Fernandes are also carrying fitness concerns, with both players reported as injury doubts, although their availability could be assessed closer to kick-off.

Ruan and Hwang Ui-jo are expected to feature in attack, while Ianis Hagi and Gaïus Makouta could provide creativity from midfield as Alanyaspor look to improve their scoring record.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from an injury and is expected to remain sidelined, while Chidozie Awaziem is also a doubt.

Palut could therefore retain much of the side that started against Besiktas, with Enis Destan and Jackson Muleka expected to provide the attacking threat, while Deniz Turuc and Jean-Luc Dompe could play important roles in supporting the forwards.

Alanyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Victor; Hadergjonaj, Lima, Ozyurt, Ozdemir; Makouta, Maestro; Kaya, Hagi, Ruan; Hwang Ui-jo.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Oguz, Yazgili, Bosluk, Masuaku; Turuc, Toth, Ibrahimoglu, Dompe; Destan, Muleka.

Alanyaspor are struggling to produce consistent performances at both ends of the pitch, but their home advantage could prove vital against a Konyaspor side that has also experienced a difficult run of results.

However, the home side’s defensive problems should give the away side’s opportunities to find the net, and with both teams desperate to avoid another defeat, we expect a closely contested encounter to finish level.

AC Milan will be without another defender in Greece tomorrow, with news emerging about Davide Bartesaghi being absent for the clash.

According to MilanNews, the Rossoneri will also be without Davide Bartesaghi, who is suffering from a bout of peritendinitis. The young Italian – going off brief searches – could be out for two weeks to six at most, but there’s no more information offered on the concern and its severity.

Recent findings suggest that of course, the best-case scenario is that it’s a precautionary absence and he’s back for this weekend’s game. However, there’s no information on the matter just yet.

All that is known, though, is that the Diavolo are now up to nine injuries at this moment, with Bartesaghi joining Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers, Strahinja Pavlovic, Modric, Camarda and Pietro Terracciano.

It’s a pretty brutal list, indeed and it makes you realise how limited Milan are on the flanks, which is perhaps why another left-back could be signed in January.

Caykur Rizespor will look to extend their recent improvement when they welcome Kasimpasa to the Caykur Didi Stadium on Friday.

The hosts are 10th in the Turkish Super Lig table with 17 points from 12 matches, while the Apaches sit fifth on 23 points, with the visitors arriving in Rize in a stronger position after an impressive run of results.

Rizespor head into Friday's fixture with renewed confidence after collecting back-to-back victories against Erzurumspor and Amedspor, having endured a difficult spell during October.

Their latest success was a 2-0 away win over Amed SK, with Ali Sowe scoring both goals to take his league tally to six, as the Black Sea Sparrowhawk became the first side to claim a league victory at Diyarbakir Stadium this season.

That result followed a 2-1 home victory over Erzurumspor, while they had previously played out a goalless draw away to Kocaelispor.

However, the Black Sea side's recent recovery should be considered alongside the problems they experienced earlier in the campaign, having suffered defeats against Corum, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor before beginning their current three-game unbeaten run.

They will look to build on that form against a side they beat 3-0 in their last meeting, while they can also take encouragement from recording their first home victory of the season after losing their opening four league games at Caykur Didi Stadium.

Kasimpasa, meanwhile, have put together an impressive sequence of results and arrive in Rize having won four of their last five league matches, with their only dropped points during that period coming in a 2-2 draw against Besiktas.

The visitors followed that draw with a 2-0 victory away to Gaziantep before recording a 2-1 win over Alanyaspor in their most recent league outing, with Adrian Benedyczak scoring twice, including a late penalty to secure all three points.

The Apaches are now unbeaten in their last six matches across all competitions, winning five of those games, including a 3-1 victory over Corluspor in the Turkish Cup.

The visitors will head into this fixture with added confidence from their recent record at this ground, having avoided defeat in their last three away games against Rizespor, drawing once and winning the previous two.

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

Industry observers note that for Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

It has been revealed that “What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

“We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

In a recent development, “We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”.

Both teams are struggling with injuries….

Recent findings suggest that “Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

It has been revealed that “Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

“He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a newly introduced study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • According to recent reports, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.
  • "It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," stated the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a newly introduced study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

According to recent reports, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," stated the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

Industry observers note that it is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

Recent findings suggest that and even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's camp issue joint statement after contract pressure controversy

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.
  • Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.
  • The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.

The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.

Those remarks prompted criticism from global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the German champions of pursuing a "coordinated strategy" to pressure Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract discussions.

However, Bayern have now taken a significant step towards addressing the controversy. Following a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, the club and Musiala's agency, 11WINS, published a statement emphasising their shared commitment to the player's recovery and clarifying an vital detail about his medical history.

The announcement comes less than a week after Musiala returned to action during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, having missed almost two months through injury.

In a statement published on their official website on Wednesday, Bayern confirmed that discussions with Musiala's management had taken place the previous day.

"A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday)," the club declared.

Recent findings suggest that "For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.".

The statement also addressed speculation surrounding the timing of the midfielder's neurological symptoms, which became public earlier this year.

Bayern and 11WINS confirmed that Musiala underwent his first examination for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they initially appeared.

Crucially, that examination took place more than two months after the Germany international signed his contract extension until June 2030 on February 14, 2025.

The clarification establishes that the medical concerns arose after the agreement was completed, addressing speculation about whether the condition had been known when the lucrative deal was negotiated.

Bayern added that the examination had been conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department.

The statement concluded by confirming that the two parties had agreed to maintain contact and continue discussions "in a spirit of partnership and trust".

According to Sky Germany, Musiala's representatives Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschaffl attended Tuesday's meeting with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer and sporting director Max Eberl.

Notably, honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, whose earlier comments contributed to the controversy, were not present.

The joint statement represents a change in tone following several weeks of increasingly public discussion about Musiala's situation.

Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge had all raised questions about the potential consequences if the attacking midfielder failed to recover his previous form.

Rummenigge was particularly outspoken after Friday's draw with Cologne, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial terms of Musiala's contract if his performances did not justify the sums involved.

Those comments attracted criticism from FIFPRO, which argued that the club's senior figures were placing unnecessary pressure on a player dealing with significant health concerns.

The union called for contractual matters to be handled privately and emphasised the importance of respecting agreements already signed by both parties.

Further questions emerged following a report by Suddeutsche Zeitung about a meeting between Hoeness and Musiala's agent during the summer.

According to the German newspaper, Hoeness believed there had been a verbal understanding that the midfielder's contract could be revisited if his condition prevented him from returning to his former level.

Musiala's representatives reportedly interpreted that discussion differently, understanding only that the parties could hold further talks if the player's situation failed to improve.

Tuesday's meeting did not produce any announced agreement to alter the contract.

Indeed, Eberl told Sky Germany that salary matters had not been discussed, with the immediate focus instead placed on supporting Musiala's return.

The sporting director also expressed confidence that the midfielder could regain his best form, stressing the need to give him time without additional pressure.

Musiala's contract remains valid until 2030, and neither Bayern nor his representatives have announced any changes to its terms.

The joint statement therefore provides an crucial clarification about the circumstances surrounding the original agreement, while leaving the longer-term contractual questions unresolved.

Winner on the field (1-0) against Morocco, Senegal was then deprived of its title by the CAF appeal jury, which awarded the victory on the green carpet to the host country following the incidents that occurred during the match. But the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) finally returned the trophy to Sadio Mané’s teammates.

The day after this decision, the Confederation of African Football revealed the three finalists for the 2026 African Ballon d’Or. Unsurprisingly, Senegal and Morocco are largely represented. CAF selected two Senegalese internationals, Sadio Mané and Pape Gueye, as well as three Moroccans: Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismaël Saibari.

An absentee, however, causes a lot of talk. This is Ismaïla Sarr, the Crystal Palace winger, who is not among the finalists. The Senegalese nevertheless had a remarkable season, winning the Conference League with his club. Top scorer in the competition with nine goals, he was also named best player of the event.

The duel between Senegal and Morocco also continues in the other categories. For the trophy for the best young African player of the year, the Moroccan Ayyoub Bouaddi and the Senegalese Ibrahim Mbaye will compete with the Ivorian Yan Diomandé. Finally, Cape Verde joins the two CAN 2025 finalists among the contenders for the title of best African selection of the year. The winners will be unveiled on December 2.

Tech Report: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 80 min read (16080 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~80 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7.
  • It has been revealed that histone H3 lysine 9 (H3 K9) trimethylation, a canonical post-translational modification of constitutive heterochromatin, is known to spread over large genomic territories and repress gene expression9.
  • According to recent reports, the vertebrate clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus provides a striking example of a large gene family whose expression has been proposed to require escape from a heterochromatic environment10,11,12,13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

It has been revealed that histone H3 lysine 9 (H3 K9) trimethylation, a canonical post-translational modification of constitutive heterochromatin, is known to spread over large genomic territories and repress gene expression9. These defining properties of heterochromatin were recognized in classic position–effect variegation studies in Drosophila during the 1930s, in which euchromatic genes placed near domains with trimethylated H3 K9 (H3K9me3) became transcriptionally silenced1,2. However, subsequent discovery of genes whose expression depends on their residence within heterochromatin revealed that this conflict is not absolute. For example, expression of the light (lt) and rolled (rl) genes in flies requires their position within pericentromeric heterochromatin3,4,5. In mice and humans, proper expression of olfactory receptor (OR) and KRAB domain-containing zinc-finger protein (KZFP) genes also depends on H3K9me3 heterochromatin6,7. These ‘escapee’ genes suggest the existence of specialized regulatory strategies that allow transcription to occur within, or despite, heterochromatin, raising fundamental questions about when heterochromatin facilitates versus restrains gene expression.

According to recent reports, the vertebrate clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus provides a striking example of a large gene family whose expression has been proposed to require escape from a heterochromatic environment10,11,12,13. Pcdh genes are expressed predominantly in neurons, where they govern neuronal self–non-self discrimination and circuit formation8. In individual neurons, only a small subset of Pcdh genes are expressed, whereas most remain silent8. Because selection of Pcdh genes is random and combinatorial14,15,16,17, this process generates extraordinary cell surface protein isoform diversity that marks each neuron with a unique identity, or ‘barcode’. Neurites presenting the same Pcdh barcode recognize and avoid one another, thereby preventing self-adhesion, whereas neurites presenting distinct Pcdh barcodes do not self-recognize and can interact18,19,20. Consistent with their critical role in neural circuit assembly, genetic variants in Pcdh genes are associated with neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder21,22 and schizophrenia23.

It has been revealed that in mice, there are 58 Pcdh genes distributed across three tandemly arranged clusters—α (Pcdha), β (Pcdhb) and γ (Pcdhg)—spanning roughly 1 megabase of DNA on chromosome 18 (ref. 24) (Fig. 1a). Pcdha genes are regulated by the HS5-1 enhancer located downstream of the Pcdha cluster, whereas Pcdhb and Pcdhg genes are regulated by the HS18-22 and HS16-17 enhancers, respectively, located downstream of the Pcdhg cluster25 (Fig. 1a). The Pcdha and Pcdhg genes are further subdivided into ‘alternate’ and ‘c-type’ isoforms24 (Fig. 1a). Pcdh genes and their promoters are marked by H3 K9 trimethylation and CpG DNA methylation (5mC)10,13,26. Stochastic Pcdh gene choice requires promoter DNA demethylation driven by cohesin-mediated enhancer–promoter interactions, with promoter demethylation leading to CTCF binding and sustained transcription of the respective Pcdh gene10,13,15,27,28. Although these findings have identified how Pcdh promoters escape DNA methylation, they do not address how euchromatic Pcdh enhancers navigate H3K9me3 heterochromatin to activate silent Pcdh promoters. Several questions remain unanswered. Specifically, do stochastic enhancer–promoter interactions occur within heterochromatin? Is Pcdh transcription carried out within a heterochromatic environment otherwise programmed to suppress gene activity, or must Pcdh loci escape this environment to transcribe? And, does heterochromatin contribute to the stochasticity of Pcdh promoter choice?

According to recent reports, to answer these questions, we sought a single-molecule view of Pcdh locus architecture during development that included the positioning of active and inactive promoters. Until now, most insights into this relationship have come from bulk genomic analyses. At a locus where only a few genes are active while most remain silent, bulk measurements mainly reflect the non-chosen genes, effectively averaging out the features of the chosen ones. To circumvent this limitation, we used optical reconstruction of chromatin architecture (ORCA), a single-molecule chromatin tracing assay29, in olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) of the mouse olfactory epithelium (OE). We selected OSNs for three reasons. First, they undergo multiple stages of development and constantly regenerate, such that each stage is present within the OE simultaneously. Second, Pcdh gene expression is developmentally regulated during OSN maturation15,20, with approximately one gene per cluster expressed from each allele in mature OSNs (mOSNs) (Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 1a–c). Third, stochastic expression of Pcdh genes has a critical role in OSN axon wiring and odour map formation20,30,31.

According to recent reports, we designed ORCA probes that tile the Pcdh locus in 90 10-kilobase bins, omitting repetitive and GC-poor regions (Fig. 1a). ORCA probes were validated in OE sections from mice in which mOSNs were genetically labelled (Extended Data Fig. 2a). We visualized ORCA data as contact frequency matrices, which depict the frequency that each pair of locus positions (bins along the Pcdh locus) falls within a specified three-dimensional (3D) distance across all imaged traces. We set this threshold near the average distance between adjacent locus positions in an experiment. The contact frequency map obtained from ORCA correlated strongly with chromosome conformation capture Hi-C data of the same genomic bins from sorted mOSNs (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c, Pearson’s r = 0.87), and the correlation remained high across a sweep of ORCA contact thresholds (Extended Data Fig. 2d). ORCA data from whole OE tissue also remained consistent across separate experiments (Extended Data Fig. 2e,f, Pearson’s r = 0.98) and revealed good detection efficiency across locus positions (Extended Data Fig. 2g). These results demonstrate that ORCA faithfully captures Pcdh locus architecture.

To study how Pcdh locus architecture changes during Pcdh gene activation and neuronal maturation, we combined ORCA imaging of Pcdh DNA with RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) labelling of the five major OSN developmental cell stages: horizontal basal cells (HBCs), globose basal cells (GBCs), immediate neuronal precursors (INPs), immature OSNs (iOSNs) and mOSNs (Fig. 1c). This lineage spawns from the mitotic HBC population located near the basal surface of the OE. As OSNs progress along their developmental axis, these cells migrate towards the apical surface of the OE (Fig. 1c). RNA labelling of marker genes for each stage reflected this basal-to-apical migration (Fig. 1d). We also stained samples with fluorescently tagged wheat germ agglutinin (WGA), a lectin that binds cell membranes, to obtain 3D segmentations of cells in the OE (Extended Data Fig. 3a). We mapped both RNA and Pcdh DNA puncta to these segmentations, then classified ORCA traces (that is, individual DNA paths) into different developmental stages on the basis of the RNA signal of the cells in which they resided (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c).

The contact frequency maps for each stage of OSN development illustrated two trends. First, stripes denoting contacts between Pcdh enhancers and their target promoters became more prominent as cells matured (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 1d–f). Second, contacts between locus positions containing Pcdhb genes and the alternate genes from the Pcdha and Pcdhg clusters, as well as the 60-kilobase stretch upstream of the Pcdha genes, increased (Fig. 1e,f). Subtracting the contact frequency map of each developmental stage from the mOSN map emphasized that these inter-cluster contacts constituted the most pronounced changes in locus architecture over development (Fig. 1e).

Sources indicate that the formation of these inter-cluster contact domains was reminiscent of the checkerboard pattern created by compartmentalization of active and repressed chromatin domains seen on Hi-C maps32. Given that this compartmentalization is mainly driven by homotypic interactions between heterochromatic regions of the genome, we hypothesized that the locus regions engaging in these contacts would have histone marks characteristic of heterochromatin. To investigate this possibility, we performed quantitative native chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (nChIP–seq) for H3K9me3 in FACS-isolated HBCs and mOSNs. In HBCs, the Pcdh locus was lightly coated in H3K9me3, with H3K9me3 levels increasing roughly threefold in mOSNs (Fig. 1g,h). Furthermore, in mOSNs, two major stretches of enriched H3K9me3 emerged separated by regions devoid of H3K9me3 between and beyond them (Fig. 1g). Specifically, the DNA regions of the Pcdh locus that engaged in inter-cluster contacts over OSN development became heavily coated with H3K9me3, whereas regions of the locus containing Pcdh c-type genes and enhancers remained free of H3K9me3 (Fig. 1e,g). We hereafter refer to the H3K9me3-marked chromatin regions engaging in inter-cluster contacts as the ‘heterochromatin domain’ of the Pcdh locus. This definition indicates the spatial arrangement of the regions within the Pcdh locus that are marked by H3K9me3 in OSNs. We refer to the regions of the locus not marked by H3K9me3 containing Pcdh c-type genes and enhancers as euchromatin.

In a recent development, to understand the positioning of the heterochromatin domain within the architecture of the Pcdh locus, we calculated the distance of each locus position to the geometric centre of its respective trace and examined the median over all traces across each stage of development. All locus positions moved closer to the geometric centre as cells matured, indicating a general compaction of the locus (Fig. 1i). Layered on top of this trend, locus positions belonging to the heterochromatin domain moved closest to the centre (Fig. 1i, boxed regions), whereas euchromatic regions remained further in the periphery. To better quantify the degree of compaction of the heterochromatin domain, we measured its radius of gyration (Rg), a metric commonly used to describe the volume of a polymer, and found that Rg decreases as neurons mature (Fig. 1j). Surprisingly, as compaction increases, so does the number of genes expressed per cell from within the domain (Fig. 1j). We further visualized these changes in locus architecture by plotting individual traces coloured by regions that become heterochromatic or euchromatic over development and by examining single-molecule distance maps (Fig. 1k and Extended Data Fig. 4). Despite heterogeneity across traces, the formation of the domain was evident: in HBCs, both regions tended to occupy large and intermixed volumes, whereas in mOSNs, the regions segregated, with heterochromatin forming a dense, more centrally located domain and euchromatin occupying more open volumes in the periphery (Fig. 1k and Extended Data Fig. 4).

Overall, these results indicate that in neural stem cells, the Pcdh locus is lightly coated with H3K9me3 heterochromatin, yet open and intermixed, with a compact heterochromatin domain forming in its centre as cells mature into post-mitotic neurons (Fig. 1l). Counterintuitively, the formation of this compact structure coincides with activation of Pcdh genes (Fig. 1j).

These results could be explained by the presence of two distinct subpopulations—actively transcribing loci that transiently lose heterochromatin and silent loci that do not. Alternatively, actively transcribing loci could retain heterochromatin and their compacted architecture. Because our bulk measurements of H3K9me3 by nChIP–seq could not distinguish between these two possibilities, we turned to stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) to measure H3K9me3 in single cells. We combined STORM for H3K9me3 with RNA FISH labelling of Pcdh isoforms and OSN cell types, as well as ORCA imaging of DNA, to test for colocalization of heterochromatin with transcribing Pcdh alleles (Fig. 2a). We used RNA probes against 11 Pcdh isoforms and confirmed their specificity for their target isoforms in vitro (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b).

Recent findings suggest that overlaying Pcdh RNA staining on Pcdh DNA loci labelled by ORCA revealed DNA traces that colocalized with RNA puncta (Extended Data Fig. 6a). By measuring distances between Pcdh loci and Pcdh RNA puncta, we identified a data-driven distance threshold below which RNA transcripts could be classified as nascent (Extended Data Fig. 6b,c). RNA puncta within this threshold were brighter than those beyond it, consistent with nascent transcriptional bursting33 (Extended Data Fig. 6d).

We then examined the spatial relationship between transcribing Pcdh DNA loci and H3K9me3 STORM signal in mOSNs. Remarkably, we observed many examples of nascent transcription occurring at Pcdh loci that colocalized with H3K9me3 STORM (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 7a). Plotting the ORCA traces of these loci alongside H3K9me3 STORM localizations revealed transcribing promoters spatially residing within heterochromatin (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 7a).

It has been revealed that to assess whether STORM captured a nuclear enrichment of H3K9me3 over the Pcdh locus, we quantified the number of H3K9me3 localizations surrounding Pcdh loci relative to randomized positions within the same nuclei. The median number of H3K9me3 localizations detected around Pcdh DNA loci exceeded that of randomized positions in 999 of 1,000 simulations (empirical P = 0.002) (Fig. 2c). We performed the same analyses on Tex15 loci, which are not marked by H3K9me3 as assayed by bulk nChIP–seq (Extended Data Fig. 7b–d). We used Tex15 nascent RNA transcripts as proxies for Tex15 DNA positions (Extended Data Fig. 7c,d). In contrast to Pcdh loci, Tex15 loci did not show an enrichment for H3K9me3 (empirical P = 0.292) (Extended Data Fig. 7d). Furthermore, we observed more Tex15 loci lacking any H3K9me3 signal compared with Pcdh loci (Extended Data Fig. 7e).

Sources indicate that we next asked whether Pcdh transcription was associated with reduced local H3K9me3 signal and domain compaction by first dividing loci into those with or without detectable nascent transcription, the latter of which we hereafter refer to as non-transcribing. We then measured the number of H3K9me3 STORM localizations around these loci and the Rg of their heterochromatin domains by ORCA. Surprisingly, transcribing Pcdh loci had slightly higher H3K9me3 STORM signal and slightly more compact heterochromatin domains relative to non-transcribing loci (Fig. 2d,e). Furthermore, transcription of individual Pcdh genes was associated neither with a change in H3K9me3 STORM signal around transcribing promoters, at the resolution of our assay, nor with a change in heterochromatin domain compaction (Fig. 2f,g).

Overall, these analyses indicate that transcription of Pcdh loci can occur in H3K9me3-rich nuclear territories and does not disrupt the heterochromatin domain of the locus.

It has been revealed that these data prompted us to further evaluate features of a transcribing Pcdh locus. To do that, we expanded the design of our RNA probes to a total of 31 Pcdh genes that showed appreciable staining and specificity (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). We noted that nascently transcribing RNA puncta often colocalized with other Pcdh RNAs of the same cluster (Fig. 3a), and more nascent puncta were detected for progressively downstream isoforms at the Pcdha and Pcdhg, but not Pcdhb, clusters (Fig. 3b). Meanwhile, mature transcript levels measured by bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) remained relatively flat across all clusters (Fig. 3b). We reasoned that these results could reflect nascent transcription of Pcdha and Pcdhg genes that reads through downstream isoforms (Fig. 3c). Yet, the number of nascent Pcdh RNAs detected at a locus was not associated with changes in heterochromatin domain Rg (Fig. 3d), indicating that this putative transcriptional readthrough occurs without domain decompaction.

According to recent reports, to identify features of locus architecture associated with transcription, we subtracted the contact frequency maps of non-transcribing loci from the maps of transcribing loci in mOSNs. This revealed an enrichment of enhancer–promoter contacts in transcribing loci (Fig. 3e–g), which was further supported by an increase in transcription probability as a function of enhancer–promoter proximity (Extended Data Fig. 8). For Pcdha and Pcdhg genes, these enhancer–promoter contact enrichments included promoters upstream of the transcribing isoform, and the magnitude of enrichment experienced by each promoter diminished when filtering on transcription of progressively downstream isoforms (Fig. 3e,g). By contrast, Pcdhb promoters had more local enhancer-contact enrichments upon transcription (Fig. 3f).

Together, these data indicate that at the Pcdha and Pcdhg clusters, transcription of chosen promoters reads through downstream genes. This pattern is consistent with splicing of Pcdha and Pcdhg variable exons to three small constant exons located 3′ of these clusters34, and was not observed at the Pcdhb cluster, which lacks constant exons. Furthermore, these data indicate that Pcdh gene choice is driven by highly specific enhancer–promoter interactions across this multi-gene, multi-enhancer locus.

It has been revealed that we next asked where Pcdh transcription and enhancer–promoter interactions occur within the spatial architecture of the locus (Fig. 1l) and, in particular, whether transcribing promoters remain within or exit the heterochromatin domain. To assess the positioning of transcribing promoters, we measured the distances between promoters and heterochromatic locus positions in the presence and absence of transcription in mOSNs (Fig. 4a). These distances did not change during transcription (Fig. 4a). On the other hand, distances between promoters and euchromatic locus positions decreased during transcription (Fig. 4a). This effect seemed driven by decreased distances between promoters and enhancers upon transcription (Fig. 4b). These results indicate that enhancer–promoter contacts associated with transcription bring euchromatic locus positions closer to the heterochromatin domain, but neither these contacts nor transcription itself cause transcribing promoters to exit the domain. Plotting transcription probability as a function of a promoter’s distance to the heterochromatin centre supported this conclusion, as promoters were most likely to be transcribing at distances within the median Rg of the heterochromatin domain (Fig. 4c).

Recent findings suggest that to further dissect the positioning of enhancers and promoters relative to the heterochromatin and euchromatin compartments of the locus during contact, we calculated the distances of each locus position to the centre of the heterochromatin domain (dHC) and the centre of the euchromatic region housing the cluster-specific enhancer(s) of that position (dEC) (Extended Data Fig. 9a). We examined Pcdhb16 as a case study. In non-transcribing traces and transcribing traces without enhancer–promoter contacts, Pcdhb16 was closer to the heterochromatin centre than the euchromatin centre, whereas its enhancer HS18-22 indicated the opposite relationship (Extended Data Fig. 9a). In Pcdhb16-transcribing traces with enhancer–promoter contacts, Pcdhb16 and its enhancer HS18-22 were more equidistant to the two centres (Extended Data Fig. 9a). Further evaluation of the equidistant state showed that the dHC of both promoter and enhancer decreased during contact, but that the enhancer dHC decreased by a greater magnitude (Extended Data Fig. 9b), consistent with promoters remaining within the heterochromatin domain during contact and the enhancers approaching the domain to engage promoters (Fig. 4a,b). Extending these analyses to all other Pcdh genes stained for showed similar positionings of transcribing Pcdh promoters and cognate enhancers relative to their compartment centres: when in contact, promoters and enhancers became more equidistant to the two centres; when not in contact, promoters were closer to the heterochromatin centre than the euchromatin centre, whereas enhancers were closer to the euchromatin centre (Extended Data Fig. 9c,d). Quantifying the percentage of transcribing traces with and without enhancer–promoter contacts revealed the latter state to be more prevalent (Extended Data Fig. 9e), indicating that promoters transcribe at positions closer to the heterochromatin centre, and that Pcdh transcription can be sustained in the absence of enhancer engagement.

Individual traces reflected the above behaviours. Transcribing promoters remained within the heterochromatin domain, and enhancers approached the domain to engage promoters (Fig. 4d).

Lastly, we investigated the genome folding mechanisms that establish Pcdh locus architecture and how this architecture supports stochastic Pcdh gene choice. The wild-type (WT) locus architecture is defined by stripes corresponding to enhancer–promoter contacts and by inter-cluster contacts within the heterochromatin domain (Fig. 1e). To abolish enhancer–promoter contacts, we conditionally removed Rad21, the kleisin subunit of the cohesin protein complex, using an Omp-ires-cre;Rad21fl/fl;tdTomatofl/fl (Rad21 cKO) mouse (Extended Data Fig. 10a). To perturb heterochromatin compaction, we conditionally deleted Setdb1, the SET domain bifurcated histone methyltransferase 1, which catalyses di- and trimethylation of H3K9, using an Omp-ires-cre;Setdb1fl/fl;tdTomatofl/fl (Setdb1 cKO) mouse (Extended Data Fig. 10a). We confirmed knockout of Rad21 and Setdb1 in mOSNs by immunofluorescence (Extended Data Fig. 10b), then performed ORCA in both mouse models.

Rad21 deletion abolished enhancer–promoter contacts as evidenced by a loss of stripes (Fig. 5a), consistent with previous reports10,13,15,27. By contrast, Setdb1 deletion resulted in a loss of inter-cluster contacts (Fig. 5a), which was accompanied by an approximately 40% reduction of H3K9me3 over the heterochromatin domain (Fig. 5b,c and Extended Data Fig. 10c). Furthermore, separation between heterochromatic and euchromatic regions of the locus increased in Rad21 cKO but decreased in Setdb1 cKO (Fig. 5d), whereas the relative size of the heterochromatin domain increased in Setdb1 cKO but decreased in Rad21 cKO (Fig. 5e).

Each black dot represents one biological replicate (WT: n = 6; Setdb1 cKO: n = 3). Data were combined across three independent experiments for WT and two independent experiments for Setdb1 cKO.
