DPT was run using a cell in the glandular region of the tumour as a ‘root cell’, representing its most unperturbed region.

Sources indicate that the use of human CRC organoid cultures was approved as part of the iCAN Precision Medicine Flagship study reviewed by the HUS Ethical Committee and is executed based on a HUS research permit (4.5.2023 §38 (HUS/223/2023)), a Findata data permit (THL/1338/14.02.00/2022) and material transfer agreements with Helsinki Biobank (HBP20210170) and Finnish Hematology and Registry Biobank FHRB (12.5.2022). The underlying PANORG study collecting the samples to the iCAN Flagship was approved by the ethical committee of the Helsinki and Uusimaa hospital district and study site institutional review boards (PANORG ethical approval HUS/390/2021, HUS approval HUS/69/2022). The study participants provided written, informed consent for the protocols. Organoids were maintained in a mixture of 60% LWRN medium (originally established in ref. 78) and 40% human basal medium supplemented with rhEGF (R&D, 236-EG, 100 ng ml−1); LWRN was replaced with Advanced DMEM (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for no-WNT conditions. Organoids were subjected to single-cell sequencing and selected to harbour APC and TP53 mutations for the studies here.

It has been revealed that patient-derived CRC organoids were cultured in Matrigel or collagen (drug treatment experiment), after which single-cell suspensions were generated by incubation with cell recovery solution (30 min at 4 °C; Corning) followed by digestion with TrypLE Express Enzyme (5 min at 37 °C; Invitrogen). After washing with ice-cold DMEM, single cells were counted using Luna-II automated cell counter (Logos Biosystems) and loaded on a microwell cartridge of the BD Rhapsody Express system (BD) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Single-cell whole-transcriptome analysis libraries were prepared according to the manufacturer’s instructions using the BD Rhapsody WTA Reagent kit (BD, 633802) and sequenced on the Illumina NextSeq 500 system using the High Output Kit v2.5 (150 cycles, Illumina) for 2 × 75 bp paired-end reads with 8 bp single index aiming sequencing depth of >20,000 reads per cell for each sample.

UMI, complex barcode, and sample tags were extracted from raw reads and demultiplexed using a custom script (rhapsody-demultiplex; https://github.com/Bioinformatics-Service-MPI-Munster/scrna-tools). Reads were mapped using STAR (v.2.7.10a)79 (--soloType CB_UMI_Complex --soloCellFilter None --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate --soloFeatures GeneFull_Ex50pAS --soloAdapterSequence NNNNNNNNNGTGANNNNNNNNNGACA --soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM --soloCBposition 2_0_2_8 2_13_2_21 3_1_3_9 --soloUMIposition 3_10_3_17 --soloCBwhitelist BD_CLS1_v2_draft.txt BD_CLS2_v2_draft.txt BD_CLS3_v2_draft.txt --runRNGseed 1 --soloMultiMappers EM --readFilesCommand zcat --outSAMattributes NH HI AS nM NM MD jM jI MC ch CB UB GX GN). Raw counts were imported as AnnData (v.0.10.7)80 objects in Python (v.3.9.11). We removed low-complexity barcodes using the knee plot method (1,500–3,000 counts per cell) and further filtered out cells with a high mitochondrial mRNA percentage (>50%). Doublets were predicted with scrublet (v.0.2.3)81. Finally, each sample’s gene expression matrix was normalized using scran (v.1.26.2)82, with Leiden clustering83 input at resolution 0.5.

According to recent reports, at this stage, the samples were merged with scanpy (v.1.10.1)75. For 2D embedding, expression values were cell cycle regressed using sc.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle with G2M and S-phase gene lists from ref. 84 and sc.pp.regress_out. The expression matrix was subset to the 3,000 most highly variable genes (sc.pp.highly_variable_genes, flavor=“seurat”). We calculated and selected the top 100 PCs (sc.tl.pca), which served as basis for k-nearest neighbour calculation (sc.pp.neighbors, n_neighbors = 30). Nearest neighbours were then used as an input for UMAP layout (sc.tl.umap, min_dist = 0.3). Leiden clusters were calculated using sc.tl.leiden at resolution 0.7. Pseudotime and gene set enrichment analyses were performed as described for the spatial transcriptomics datasets. For reanalysis of the published tumour in vivo data, we chose a cell in the most stem-like cluster according to CytoTRACE analysis.

For generation of consensus gene sets, EMT gene sets (mesenchymal67, matrix remodelling68, TGFB activation (TGFB KEGG, TGFB CORE GENES/TGFB1/TGFB2)68,69, EMT activation (EMT Core Genes67, EMT Hallmark70, pEMT71, EMT-II (MP13)72) and SC gene sets (crypt base32, LGR5 intestinal SCs33, fetal8, regenerative34 and revival colonic SCs52) were merged and overlapping genes within and across gene sets were removed to generate the Core-EMT, Core-CBC and Core-RegSC gene sets.

Recent findings suggest that all cells in the dataset were scored for the Core-EMT, Core-CBC and Core-RegSC gene sets using the Scanpy sc.tl.score_genes function. The scores were then converted to a per-dataset rank rescaled to [0, 1]. Cells were then ordered across the CBC to RegSC–EMT axis as a composite_trajectory = (RegSC_rank01 + EMT_rank01 − CBC_rank01 + 1)/3. Cells with composite_trajectory in the top 30% of the per-dataset distribution were classified hybrid.

Sources indicate that for distribution across the EMT–RegSC axis, two curated marker panels were scored per hybrid cell with sc.tl.score_genes (random_state = 0): a RegSC-pole panel (GPRC5A, TSPAN1, PDZK1IP1, ANXA1, ANXA3, S100A6, S100A11, LCN2, SAA1, SAA2, KRT16, KRT17, SPP1, CD44, EMP1 and TACSTD2) and an EMT pole panel (SNAI1, SNAI2, ZEB1, ZEB2, TWIST1, TWIST2, VIM, FN1, S100A4, ACTA2, MMP14, PLAU, PLAUR, SERPINE1, TIMP1). Each panel score was z-scored within its dataset, and the pole axis was defined as axis_pole = z(score_EMT_pole) − z(score_RegSC_pole). The pole-axis shift among hybrid cells was computed as Cliff’s δ = 2 × U/(n_c × n_Unt) − 1, where U is the Mann–Whitney U statistic of axis pole over the two hybrid groups. δ ∈ [−1, +1]; δ < 0 represents that hybrid cells of c are shifted toward the regenerative pole relative to untreated-hybrid cells, δ > 0 represents that hybrid cells of c are shifted toward the EMT pole. By default, untreated sits at δ = 0.

Hydrogel scaffolds were engineered as described previously42,85. A PDMS stamp (see below) with a crypt-mimicking array of pillar topography was placed in the central top reservoir of the chip. To generate the ECM for the chip, bovine TeloCol-6 type I collagen solution (5225-50mL, Advanced Biomatrix) was neutralized according to the manufacturer’s instructions and then mixed with Matrigel (356231, Corning) at a 75/25 (v/v) ratio. After gel injection through gel-loading port, hydrogel was polymerized at 37 °C, 5% CO2 (hereafter referred to as incubator) for 15 min. After ECM polymerization, all chip reservoirs were topped up with PBS or cell culture medium.

It has been revealed that stamps featuring crypt-mimicking microtopography were fabricated from PDMS by replica moulding of 2PP-printed models. First, arrays of colon crypt-mimicking micropillars were designed in Autodesk Fusion. Several topographies were tested and optimized, the final microtopography design consists of the slightly conical pillars, ranging from 50 to 120 µm in diameter (top to bottom) and 700 µm in height. The 3D model was printed using a NanoOne (UpNano) 2PP printer on glass coverslips with UpPhoto resin and a ×10/0.4 NA objective. To generate a master mould with inverted topography, the printed structures were plasma-activated and silanized overnight using vapour-phase trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane (Sigma-Aldrich). PDMS (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning; 10:1 base-to-curing agent ratio) was poured over the master, degassed under vacuum, and cured at 80 °C for 12 h. The resulting PDMS replica was cut, plasma-activated and silanized overnight as above. This PDMS negative was then used repeatedly as a mould for casting final PDMS stamps using the same procedure (Sylgard 184, 10:1 ratio, cured at 80 °C for 12 h).

Organoids were dissociated using TrypLE Express (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and resuspended at 40 million cells per ml in Advanced DMEM (Thermo Fisher Scientific) supplemented with 10 µM Y27632 after which 5 µl of cell suspension was plated onto each chip. Cells were allowed to settle for 1 h in a cell culture incubator, after which the chips were filled with Y27632-supplemented medium. The next day, Y27632 was removed and cells were cultured for 5 days. Chips were fixed in 4% PFA for 16 h at 4 °C, placed into 3D-printed custom histomoulds, filled with HistoGel (Thermo Fisher Scientific), embedded in paraffin and sectioned as described previously86. The samples were then processed for RNA in situ hybridization or immunofluorescence as described below.

In situ hybridization was performed using RNAscope technology (Advanced Cell Diagnostics) according to the manufacturer’s protocols. In brief, organoids were fixed in 4% PFA for 30 min at 37 °C, rinsed with PBS, dehydrated in a graded ethanol series and air dried. The slides were then rehydrated and 2 drops of hydrogen peroxide were added to each slide for 10 min. Primary antibodies were added and incubated overnight at 4 °C. The slides were washed and fixed with 4% PFA for 30 min at room temperature. After PBS washes, three drops of 1:15 diluted Protease Plus were added to slides and incubated for 10 min, followed by PBS washes.

It has been revealed that RNA probes were prewarmed for 10 min at 40 °C, cooled down and added onto slides. The slides were incubated with probes for 2 h at 40 °C, washed twice with wash buffer, subjected to stepwise hybridization with amplifier solutions for 15 min each at 40 °C, followed by application of blocker solutions. Finally, samples were incubated with Alexa-conjugated secondary antibodies diluted in co-detection antibody diluent for 30 min at room temperature. After washes and brief incubation with DAPI, the slides were mounted in Elvanol and imaged. The following probes were used: ANXA1-c3 465411, LGR5-c2 311021, OLFM4-c1 311041, VIM-c1 310441. Images were obtained using the Zeiss LSM980 system using ×20 air and ×40 water objectives. Channels were acquired sequentially at room temperature using Zeiss Zen Blue software (v.3.13).

Industry observers note that organoids were fixed in 4% PFA for 1 h at room temperature, permeabilized in 0.6% Triton X-100 for 30 min, blocked with 5% BSA and 5% goat serum in PBS for 2 h, after which primary antibodies were added in blocking solution and incubated overnight at 4 °C. After multiple washes in PBS, secondary Alexa Fluor-conjugated antibodies were added in 1% BSA, 1% goat serum for 2 h at room temperature. Organoids were then mounted in ProLong Gold (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The following primary antibodies were used: ANXA1 (Abcam, ab214486, 1:1,000, overnight, 4 °C), YAP1 (Santa Cruz, sc-101199, 1:500, overnight, 4 °C), active YAP (Abcam, ab205270, 1:100, overnight, 4 °C), β-catenin (Cell Marque, 224M-14, 1:100, overnight, 4 °C), SNAIL1 (Santa Cruz, sc-271977, 1:50, overnight, 4 °C), HP1α (Cell Signaling, 2616, 1:200, overnight, 4 °C), lamin A/C (Cell Signaling, 2032, 1:200, overnight, 4 °C), SOX4 (Abcam, ab236557, 1:400, overnight, 4 °C), pSMAD2/3 (Cell Signaling, 3108, 1:100, overnight, 4 °C). Images were obtained using either the Zeiss LSM980 or Nikon Yokogawa CSU-W1 system with ×20 air and ×40 water objectives. Channels were acquired sequentially at room temperature using Zeiss Zen Blue software (v.3.13) or NIS Elements (AR 5.41.01).

Recent findings suggest that to mechanically compress the organoids, organoids grown in Matrigel for 5 days were replated on top of Matrigel-coated 12–20 mm round glass coverslips and allowed to attach for 24 h. After attachment, the organoids were sandwiched with another 12–20 mm coverslip with a weight applying 200 Pa of vertical stress (generating a 45% reduction in organoid height) for 20 h.

It has been revealed that for 3D organoid imaging, single cells were first embedded in 8 mg ml−1 Matrigel and, after 4 days of culture, were transferred either to fresh Matrigel or pH-adjusted 1 mg ml−1 collagen I matrices. The organoids were treated with 5 µM TDI-011536 (MedChemExpress, HY-150042), 10 ng ml−1 TGFβ1 (StemCell Technologies, 78067.1) or both with daily medium replenishment while being live-cell imaged every 30 min with a Sartorius Incucyte S3 incubator microscope for up to 4 days.

Bright-field images were segmented using Cellpose4-SAM87 and edge detection followed by morphological gap-closing and hole-filling to obtain binary organoid masks that were imported to ImageJ (Fiji). MorphoLibJ88 was used to quantify convexity, Geodesic diameter, Geodesic elongation and organoid area that were scaled between 0 and 1 to initially classify the organoids into expanded, dispersive or cohesive classes in an unbiased manner. As the resolution of the masks was not sufficient to accurately capture surface structures, the classifications were all manually inspected further and assigned to the final classes.

RNA was isolated using the NucleoSpin RNA plus Kit (Macherey-Nagel). RNA quality was assessed using the high-sensitivity RNA Screen Tape Analysis (TapeStation, Agilent) and subsequently 500 ng of RNA was reverse transcribed applying the SuperScript IV VILO Master Mix (Thermo Fisher Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. PCR was performed using the PowerUp SYBR Green Mastermix (Thermo Fisher Scientific) on the QuantStudio5 Real-Time PCR System (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Gene expression was quantified using the ΔΔCt method with normalization to B2M. The following primers were used. B2M: forward primer, GAGTATGCCTGCCGTGTGAA; reverse primer, GCTTACATGTCTCGATCCCACT; AXIN2: forward primer, GCGCTGACGGATGATTCCAT; reverse primer, TGGGTTCTCGGGAAATGAGGT; ASCL2: forward primer, CGCCTACTCGTCGGACGACAG; reverse primer, GCCGCTCGCTCGGCTTCCG.

Industry observers note that mouse colonoscopy was performed using the TELE PACK+VET system (Karl Storz, RP101S1). Illumination was provided by a xenon light source connected through the Adapt. KST fibre-optic light cable/Xenon 100 (495KS). The system includes a camera control, air insufflation units and an integrated endoscopic video unit with built-in documentation and memory storage. Colonoscopy imaging was performed using an integrated multipurpose Hopkins Telescope (67031BA) with an outer diameter of 11.5 Fr. Images were acquired using an IMAGE1 S HX FULL HD Camera Head (TH110). Mice were anaesthetized with isoflurane and organoid fragments corresponding to 5 × 105 single cells were transplanted into the colonic submucosa using a Hamilton syringe (Hamilton, Reno, 7656-01) equipped with a transfer needle for sample loading (7770-02) and an injection needle (7803-05). The needle was carefully inserted into the colonic submucosa, and 50 µl of organoid fragments suspended in 1 mg ml−1 rat collagen type 1 (Sigma-Aldrich, C3867) supplemented with 10% Corning Matrigel (Corning, 356231) was delivered and generated a visible submucosal bleb. The mice were treated for 5 days after transplantation with the LATS kinase inhibitor TDI-011536 (MedChemExpress, HY-150042). TDI-011536 was prepared at a concentration of 5 mg ml−1 by emulsification in 10% Kolliphor HS 15 (Merck, 42966) in PBS and administered by oral gavage twice daily at a dose of 2.5 mg per kg. Vehicle-treated animals received 10% Kolliphor in PBS alone.

TGFβ1 treatment was performed using human recombinant TGFβ1 (StemCell Technologies, 78067.1) within Affi-Gel Blue beads (Bio-Rad Laboratories, 153-7301). In brief, beads were washed four times with ice-cold bi-distilled water and incubated overnight with 500 µl of 50 µg ml−1 TGFβ1 in PBS supplemented with 10 mM HEPES. TGFβ1-loaded beads were mixed with organoid fragments in collagen solution at a final proportion of 10% (v/v) before implantation. For dual-treatment experiments, animals received both TDI-011536 administration and TGFβ1-loaded beads as described above. Each treatment group consisted of four mice (n = 4). Mice were monitored three times per week, and colonoscopy imaging was performed every 2 weeks for 4 weeks before euthanasia.

It has been revealed that tissue biopsies (intestinal rolls) were fixed in 4% PFA, embedded in paraffin and sectioned. Sections were de-paraffinized using a graded alcohol series and antigen retrieval was carried out using target retrieval solution (Dako) at pH 6 or pH 9 in a pressure cooker. Unspecific binding was blocked using 5% normal goat serum, 3% BSA in PBS, after which antibodies were diluted in DAKO antibody diluent and incubated overnight in a moist chamber at 4 °C. After PBS washes, Alexa-Fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies were diluted in 1% BSA in PBS, incubated for 1 h at room temperature, after which samples were mounted in Elvanol. The following primary antibodies were used: ANXA1 (Abcam, ab214486), pSMAD2/3 (Cell Signaling, 3108) and active YAP (Abcam ab205270). Images were obtained using the Zeiss LSM980 system with ×20 air and ×40 water objectives. Channels were acquired sequentially at room temperature using Zeiss Zen Blue software (v.3.13). The tumour area was quantified using ANXA1 staining to generate a ROI mask in Fiji. The number of ROIs was used to extract the lesion number.

All animal experiments were performed in accordance with EU Directive 2010/63/EU and Finnish legislation, and were approved by the National Animal Experiment Board of Finland (ELLA) under project licence ESAVI/30305/2023. Female NOD.Cg-PrkdcscidIl2rgtm1Wjl/SzJ (NSG) mice (The Jackson Laboratory, 005557) were used at 12 weeks of age at the start of the experiment. Sample size was determined using the resource equation method (E = N − T), where N is the total number of animals and T the number of groups; with four groups of four mice (N = 16), E = 12, within the recommended range of 10–20. Mice were randomly allocated to experimental groups; no formal randomization method was used. Tumour implantation was confirmed in all mice, and animals were euthanized and dissected 4 weeks after transplantation. No mice reached the humane end-point limits defined in the licence, and no mice were excluded from the analysis.

Recent findings suggest that statistical analyses were performed using GraphPad Prism software (GraphPad, v.9) or in R (v.2023.09.1+494). Statistical significance was determined using the specific tests indicated in the corresponding figure legends. Only two-tailed tests were used. In all cases in which a test for normally distributed data was used, normal distribution was confirmed using the Kolmogorov–Smirnov test (α = 0.05). All experiments presented in the manuscript were repeated at least in three independent replicates. Automated software algorithms were used for unbiased quantification of staining intensities, sequencing data and architecture features/cell shapes in all experiments involving these techniques so blinding was not relevant. For animal experiments endoscopy and sample collection were performed in a blinded manner. For manual organoid invasion pattern classification blinding was applied during data analysis. No statistical methods were used to predetermine sample sizes. Sample size was determined based on previous experience, published literature, or to specific requirements of a given technique.

Recent findings suggest that (a) Flow chart of patient dataset and analyses (top panels). Venn diagrams summarizing the number of patients with quantified architecture in the tumour-core (CT) and invasive-margin (IM) compartments (bottom panel). (b) Number of analysed TMA cores per patient for each compartment (tumour core and invasive margin). (c) Representative images of tumour cores and invasive margins. Yellow dashed lines indicate the tumour–stroma boundary. Scale bar 200 µm. (d) Kaplan-Meier survival curves for patients stratified by nuclear circularity (high, medium, low) of tumour core (left) or invasive margin (right). P-values pairwise log-rank test. (e, f) Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models including the circularity shape descriptor, comparing stage II–III (e) or stage I (f) patients (p-values Wald). (g) Average nuclear shapes (area, circularity, and solidity) per patient, across tumour stages (patient-level permutation tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction). Half-violins show the kernel density estimate of the distribution of per-patient values. Boxplots show median, 25th–75th percentile (IQR), and 1.5×IQR whiskers. (h) Representative images of the six tumour architecture archetypes (scale bar 200 µm; architecture was quantified in 1,037 patients (a)).

In a recent development, (a) Representative invasive margin sample with heterogeneous architectures (left panel), classifier predictions, projection of three closest neighbours’ distances, and relative alignment (order). Scale bar 400 µm. (b) t-SNE embedding of features derived from the U-Net from tiles used for classifier training. (c) Precision and recall of the tile classifier for architecture classification across classes, with error bars representing the standard deviation from five-fold cross-validation. (d) Schematic representation of quantified histological features, including neighbourhood, morphological and tumour-stroma interactions features. (e) Silhouette scores of the 196 manually selected archetype cores in morphological feature space (12 features from Fig. 1f: neighbourhood, stroma, morphology), compared to size-matched random draws from the MSS cohort with matching per-class label counts (n = 1,000 permutations). Distribution of mean silhouette scores across random draws (grey histogram) with the archetype value (black dashed line; left panel). Per-class silhouette (right panel): violins show the null distribution; diamonds mark the archetype silhouette for each architectural subtype. Archetypes form tighter, better-separated clusters than random draws overall and within each class, indicating that the manual curation captured genuine, well-defined exemplars of each architectural subtype rather than arbitrary selections.

(a) Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models incorporating architecture types, with Glandular as the reference. Fragmented architecture remains significantly associated with poor survival after adjustment for other covariates. Estimated log hazard ratio (Cox regression coefficient) with 95% CI are shown; dashed vertical line at log(HR) = 0 indicates no effect (Wald tests with robust standard errors; p-values not adjusted for multiple comparisons). (b) Stacked bar plot displaying the distribution of architecture types across tumour stages, with left bars representing the tumour core and right bars representing the invasive margin. (c) Kaplan-Meier survival curves for stage II–III patients, stratified by architecture type from tumour core (CT) and invasive margin (IM). Patients with fragmented architectures exhibit poorer survival. (d) Kaplan-Meier survival curves for stage I–IV MSI patients, stratified by architecture type. (e, f) Kaplan-Meier survival curves of the validation dataset for MSS patients at stage I–IV (left) and stage II–III (right) (e) and for MSI patients at stage I–IV (f), stratified by architecture type. Validation dataset recapitulates poor survival in fragmented architecture MSS patients. (g) Sankey diagram illustrating the correspondence between CT and IM architecture classifications. (h) Distribution of the fragmentation index per TMA core, comparing values between the tumour core and invasive margin (paired sign-flip permutation test on log1p-transformed patient-level compartment means; n = 518 paired patients; boxplots show median IQR; 1.5×IQR whiskers). For all Kaplan-Meier curves p-values were from pairwise log-rank tests versus Glandular reference group.

According to recent reports, (a) Stacked bar plot of budding grade distribution across architectures in tumour cores (CT). (b) Kaplan-Meier curves with low budding (BD1) grade, stratified by tumour architecture. (c) Distribution of intratumoral budding in CT classified as fragmented (left) or between mildly and strongly fragmented (right). (d, e) Normalized distribution of histological subtypes (d) and tumour grade (e; Low: grade 1–2; High: grade 3–4) across architecture types. Patients with unknown grade excluded. (f) Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by tumour architecture in CT (high-grade, left; low-grade, right; stages II–III; MSS; age <85). (g) Heatmap showing percentage of patients classified as fragmented within grade and tumour budding category (BD1: 0-4 buds; BD2: 5-9 buds; BD3: ≥10 buds; MSS; CT; age <85). (h) Hazard ratios (log scale) for disease-specific survival in stage II–III MSS (age <85). Patients with unknown budding or grade excluded. Analysis performed separately for CT (green) and IM (pink). Estimated log hazard ratio (Cox regression coefficient) with 95% CI; dashed vertical line at log(HR) = 0 indicates no effect, Wald tests with robust standard errors; p-values not adjusted for multiple comparisons). (i, j) Distribution of tumour location (i) and Immunoscore (j) across architecture classifications in MSS. Proportions normalized per architecture group. Brazilian goalkeeper Neto will start for Juventus in a Europa League game against Omonia FC tomorrow: ‘I’m really excited to be back on the pitch.’.

The experienced goalkeeper returned to Turin on a free transfer in September, replacing the injured Kamil Grabara.

The Poland international suffered a season-ending knee injury, urging Juventus to sign a replacement.

Neto has not played a competitive match since May 30 with Botafogo, and last played for Juventus nearly ten years ago, in May 2017, helping them beat Lazio 2-0 in a Coppa Italia Final.

In a recent development, “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team,” Neto mentioned at a press conference today, as quoted by Ilbianconero.com.

According to recent reports, “Football and life go through different cycles, and there are different people involved. I see a very healthy environment for achieving our goals, and that’s what we need to maintain: the belief that we’re on the right track.

“I was at a point where I was looking for certain things, and whatever I did in the next stage of my life had to make sense,” he added when asked about his return to Juventus.

According to recent reports, “I was looking for something that would inspire me. When this opportunity came along, I felt that. It had a different meaning. Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m very happy and satisfied. I enjoy my work, and whatever comes in the future is in God’s hands. I’m here to help, and whatever happens will happen.

Industry observers note that “We’re in a place where, wherever you look, you see so many trophies. Whether we talk about it or not, there’s no need to spell it out: we know where we are and what we represent. I’m here to try to achieve great results, and I sense the same ambition around me. Hopefully we can get there. Just like the other teams, we want to win. That’s what we’re fighting for.”.

Juventus sit fifth in the Europa League standings with ten points in four matches, but have had very different results in Serie A, where they have already lost three games from 12 and sit 6th in the table, six points behind Milan in four.

Neto, however, has plenty of confidence in his teammates.

Recent findings suggest that “Seeing and feeling the desire these lads have, with so many young players willing to contribute, is truly infectious. From my perspective, that’s a positive thing,” the 37-year-old noted.

Industry observers note that “There are key players here. We’re talking about Juve. We have the team, the desire and the determination, and hopefully we can get there.

In a recent development, “Every competition is difficult these days. We are Juventus, and whenever Juventus play, we have a responsibility to compete to win. That’s our goal. I haven’t looked at what lies ahead, because at this club you have to fight to win. That’s how it is for me, and I imagine it’s the same for everyone.

“This is a developing team with lots of young players who may be playing in this league for the first time and are still finding their feet. There can be ups and downs. The season is so long that we can’t focus solely on this moment, because in a month we might be talking about something else. My focus is always on giving 100% in training. We need to find balance and consistency.”.

Omonia FC have grabbed two wins and two defeats in four Europa League games so far and sit 18th in the table.

“It will be a difficult match. They’re a very strong team,” insisted Neto.

In a recent development, “We’ve watched them, and they counterattack with real quality. I know Fabiano from our time in Brazil. Every game in Europe is difficult, and we know the challenges involved.”.

Sources indicate that juventus’ first-choice goalkeeper Vicario will rest tomorrow. He’s on loan from Tottenham, but does he deserve to remain at Juventus long-term?

“I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper,” Neto concluded.

#105961. Tech Report: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1225 w)

Tech Report: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • In a recent development, at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • The mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

In a recent development, at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I stated here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

The mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

"[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

Sources indicate that german Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz mentioned in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

Sources indicate that given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz noted when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

In a recent development, "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," said Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

At the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that "We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she remarked.

The government is currently in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in new debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

The economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

In a recent development, germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

However, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," noted Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

It has been revealed that the so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, mentioned the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer remarked.

Sources indicate that according to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an problem in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz remarked there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a tech giant can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

According to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

It has been revealed that if the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it said in the report. "Upcoming technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

Fresh evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

In a recent development, the intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a latest study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association showed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

Arsenal are reportedly among the clubs interested in signing Matias Soule, with the Roma winger attracting significant attention from several European sides ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

The Argentine has impressed in Italy this season, and his growing reputation could put him in contention for a move to the Premier League.

According to a report from Fussball News, Arsenal are monitoring Soule alongside Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Bournemouth and Sunderland.

The 23-year-old has registered four goals and five assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as an key figure in Gian Piero Gasperini’s attacking setup.

The Gunners have been watching attacking reinforcements, and Soule’s ability to operate on the right flank while cutting inside could make him an attractive option for Mikel Arteta.

The Argentina international has impressive technical qualities, creativity and the ability to contribute in front of goal, potentially adding another dimension to Arsenal’s final third.

Arsenal are likely to face considerable competition for his signature, with Borussia Dortmund, Stuttgart, Atletico Madrid, AC Milan and Napoli also reportedly interested.

It has been revealed that however, the Italian club is in a strong negotiating position, with Soule under contract until June 2029. Roma are reportedly reluctant to lose the attacker, although financial considerations could influence their stance.

The Serie A side are believed to value him between €55 million and €60 million, significantly higher than his estimated market value of around €35 million.

While no concrete offers have reportedly been submitted, interested clubs could explore different transfer structures, including an initial loan with an obligation to buy or performance-related bonuses.

A January move remains possible, but next summer could provide a more realistic opportunity for Arsenal to pursue the Argentine if his impressive performances continue.

Soule’s versatility and attacking quality make him an intriguing target, although Arsenal would need to consider the financial implications before committing to such a significant transfer.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

According to recent reports, “I have to take the responsibility,” he said. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the strategy. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

Recent findings suggest that “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the blueprint disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight fresh signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat swiftly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

Sources indicate that newcastle and Everton meet for the second time in matter of days as the Premier League weekend concludes in the north east at St James’ Park. These teams encountered each other on Thursday night in the League Cup, where Everton won 3-1 at the Hill Dickinson to progress to the quarter-finals in that competition.

Newcastle, who won 2-0 at Crystal Palace in their last league outing, come into this game in 12th, with the chance to rise to seventh with a victory tonight. Their boss Matthias Jaissle has called on his players to use the defeat against Everton on Thursday as fuel for tonight.

In a recent development, “Now it is about taking that frustration into motivation for Monday and having that approach for the rematch,” Jaissle said. “We take it as a long-term journey, and our approach is to make progress, to see improvements. Now it is time to learn fast out of the mistakes that we just did. [There are] other phases where we can already see that we improved and this is something we can count on, we can build on, the good part. But football is also in the end about results so you need to avoid these simple mistakes.”.

Recent findings suggest that everton, who have not won in the league since a 1-0 victory over Ipswich back in September, begin the night in 14th but, like Newcastle, could rise to seventh with a win. There are just two points that separate Bournemouth in seventh and Everton in 14th. Despite getting the better of Newcastle the other night, Everton manager David Moyes has warned that game will count for nothing tonight.

“It is a different ball game,” Moyes mentioned. “Go to St James’ Park, on a Monday evening, they will get a crowd up there, you always know you are up against it. But we will go with confidence. We have played Newcastle a couple of times this year and done well, so we have to try and continue it. But Newcastle have got some really, really good players and players you have to concern yourself about.”.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton’s squad for that League Cup victory because of an unauthorised absence from training and the 31-year-old is not expected to be involved tonight.

Industry observers note that these sides were involved in a dramatic fixture on this ground last season. Everton claimed a 3-2 victory, with Thierno Barry earning them all three points in the 83rd minute, moments after Jacob Murphy had equalised for Newcastle. Despite signing three latest midfielders at a cost of more than £150m in the summer, following on from a rebuild of their attack the previous summer, the current Man United squad looks nowhere near good enough.

11 matches into the Premier League season and they have one win and lie 19th in the standings, which demonstrates how poor they have been.

Pochettino has been tasked with turning their campaign around and lifting them up the table, but his reign got off to the worst possible start when they were reduced to 10 men eight minutes in away at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, going on to lose 4-0 on Merseyside.

Aside from Casemiro, the current Red Devils' squad is the same as the one that went on a stunning run of form in the first half of 2026 to finish third behind Arsenal and Manchester City in the top flight, qualifying for the Champions League as a result.

Defence is clearly an issue too though, with only Lens conceding more goals than United's 34 this term from teams who make up the top five leagues in Europe.

The defensive rebuild was on the agenda for the summer but it appears as though it will be brought forward, as club chiefs look at signing a centre-back and left-back hybrid, or potentially even one for each position.

GIVEMESPORT senior correspondent Ben Jacobs reported on deadline day in the summer that United had made a late enquiry for Man City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri, although no move materialised.

Now, TEAMtalk claim that the Red Devils have once again reached out to their neighbours about the Algeria international, with a switch to Old Trafford remarked to hold high appeal for the former Wolves star.

According to the report, Ait-Nouri has been informed that he can leave the Etihad in January if the deal is right, but Jacobs revealed in September that United were unwilling to agree to City's demands for a loan move with an obligation to buy.

It will be interesting to see if they have changed their stance and if they would be open to a straight loan with an option, because that is something that would surely appeal to the Red Devils given there are suggestions that their budget could be limited mid-season.

Ait-Nouri has struggled to force his way into the City XI ever since joining in a deal worth up to £36m from Wolves, but he does have extensive Premier League experience, he has played in the Champions League, and he has the full-back traits that Pochettino likes.

The 25-year-old may count himself unlucky at how limited his minutes have been at the Etihad, especially this season, but he established himself as one of the best in his position during his time at Molineux previously.

While United are being linked with the likes of Antonee Robinson of Fulham and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, with Ben Jacobs naming a £75m star as another 'one to watch', Ait-Nouri is a strong option to finally provide some strong competition for Luke Shaw.

Shaw has once again shown this term that the club cannot afford to rely on his fitness, even if he could be back on the pitch soon after an eight-match absence.
